title: Association between periodontitis and coronary artery disease and the impact of periodontal therapy on the progression of coronary artery disease: a prospective, randomized controlled trial.
summary: The study investigates whether targeted treatment of gum inflammation (periodontitis) can influence the progression of cardiovascular diseases, particularly coronary artery disease. Patients with periodontitis are divided into two groups: one group receives a timely, structured periodontal treatment, while the other group initially undergoes only regular dental check-ups, with treatment provided later if necessary. Over a period of two years, changes in the coronary arteries, blood inflammatory markers, and periodontal parameters are assessed to determine whether early periodontal therapy can also reduce cardiovascular risk.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of a clinical indication for cardiac CT imaging due to suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or suspected progression of known CAD, manifested by symptoms such as stable angina pectoris or exertional dyspnea, as well as documented recent dental care, defined as regular check-ups by a primary dentist within the past two years.
Exclusion criteria:
Ongoing periodontal treatment, lack of regular dental care, inability to provide informed consent, and current pregnancy.
